prize_parts.citation: For the development of ionizable lipid nanoparticles that enable delivery of nucleic-acid medicines

statement.case_for: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a molecular-design solution with a clear chemical principle: lipids tuned to be near neutral in circulation and cationic at endosomal pH, which allows nucleic acids to be encapsulated, protected and released in the cell. This is soft-matter and pharmaceutical chemistry that changed what clinicians can actually do, giving the first approved siRNA drug and the mRNA vaccines used in billions of doses. Independent confirmation is overwhelming, so maturity is not in doubt. The 2023 Medicine prize honored nucleoside modification, the cargo, and not the carrier chemistry, so a Chemistry prize on delivery has a distinct citation. The Cullis, Anderson and Langer configuration pairs the Vancouver origin of ionizable-lipid formulation with the combinatorial lipidoid work that showed the design space could be explored systematically and generalized beyond one lipid.
statement.case_against: Credit is spread over more people than three: MacLachlan, Hope and Madden made decisive Vancouver contributions, and much of the lipid optimization that reached the clinic was done in industry. Any three-person cut is therefore contestable, and the work overlaps the topic of the 2023 Medicine prize, which some members will read as already covered. Compared with B054, the committee also has to decide whether this is a single coherent discovery or a long, distributed engineering effort.

responses.point: Linke ranks LNPs fourth and would credit Cullis, Hope and Madden, because the Vancouver group built the formulation methods and early ionizable-lipid particles, and he notes the tangle with Medicine 2023 and with patent disputes.
responses.response: I take the attribution point seriously: Hope and Madden did the early loading and formulation work, and that is the strongest argument against my own trio. I still credit Anderson and Langer because lipidoid libraries turned ionizable-lipid design from a single finding into a general chemical strategy that extended to siRNA, mRNA and other cargos, and Langer's role in delivery chemistry is broader than any one formulation. I disagree that Medicine 2023 weakens the case: Karikó and Weissman changed the nucleic acid, and the carrier is a separate chemical problem without which the nucleoside-modified mRNA would not have been deliverable. I would concede that the Cullis-Hope-Madden allocation is defensible if the committee prefers a Vancouver-centered citation.

responses.point: Sparr ranks phase separation first and LNPs second, framing LNPs as lipid self-assembly with pKa-tuned ionizable lipids and controlled formulation, with overwhelming validation and a need to distinguish them from Medicine 2023.
responses.response: I agree on the soft-matter framing and on maturity, and that gives LNPs a clear chemistry identity. Where we differ is B044. I ranked condensates sixth because the in vivo physiological relevance of phase separation is still disputed and a prize would have to leave out Pappu and Mittag, who supplied the physical theory. LNPs have no comparable dispute about whether the phenomenon is real. A condensate prize may prove right in a decade, but today I think the evidence base is firmer for delivery chemistry.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing first as a biological process rendered as a defined chemical reaction, with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli as the core, and ranks degraders second and LNPs fourth.
responses.response: I share your criterion of chemistry that turns biology into a controllable reaction, and I ranked B069 third. My hesitation is the shortness of the clinical record and the closeness to the 2020 CRISPR prize, which makes base editing look like a refinement of a recently recognized platform, whereas LNPs address a separate bottleneck. On attribution I would keep Liu alone: Komor and Gaudelli were lead trainees on his program, and adding them blurs the principle that a prize honors the conceptual driver, so I would resist your three-name version.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks Gray and Winkler first for long-range protein electron transfer, citing four decades of confirmation and a quantitative physical mechanism, and ranks degraders second with Crews, Deshaies and Handa.
responses.response: The electron-transfer work is rigorous and fully mature, and I agree that a prize built on it would be overdue rather than premature. But Marcus theory was recognized in 1992 and the main protein-specific theory by Beratan, Onuchic and Dutton falls outside the credited names, so the citation would be harder to write than yours suggests. I also ask my usual question of whether it changed what researchers and clinicians can do, and for electron tunneling the answer is mostly conceptual. I do agree with you on B054 and the Crews, Deshaies, Handa choice, and I would support it as the fallback if the committee cannot settle on LNP credit.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics first as an unmistakable, fully mature method with clean two-person credit, and ranks degraders second with Ciulli rather than Handa.
responses.response: I accept that Car and Parrinello have the cleanest attribution on the list, and that is a real virtue next to my own contested trio. My concern is that it would be a methods prize with limited reach outside theory, and its ranking depends on how much weight the committee gives to purely computational contributions. On degraders, I put Handa where you put Ciulli because the cereblon mechanism explained thalidomide and underlies the molecular glues, which have the longer clinical record. I would accept either allocation if B054 became the prize.

uncertainties: Whether the decisive ionizable-lipid credit belongs to Vancouver (Cullis, Hope, Madden), to the MIT lipidoid work (Anderson, Langer), or to industrial formulators, which I have not verified against patent or priority records.
Whether the committee treats Medicine 2023 as having already covered the mRNA vaccine story, which would reduce the room for a delivery-chemistry prize.
Whether PROTAC clinical benefit will be established soon enough to make B054 the safer choice than B036 in this cycle.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. My research overlaps with Emma Sparr's in peptide-lipid and self-assembly systems, but that is a field overlap, not a personal or institutional tie to any credited person. My postdoc mentors (Stevens, Boey) are not credited on any shortlisted ballot.
